# Adjudication Task — Chapter 443

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃443화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|열흘간의 항해는 결코 쉬운 일이 아니었다.
  6|
  7|거대 크루즈 선도 아니고 목재로 만들어진 선박에서 퀴퀴한 선실과 축축한 갑판만을 오가야 했으니까. 항구? 빠듯한 일정 탓에 앞만 보고 나아갔다.
  8|
  9|그런 사정이 있다 보니, 적천강은 물론이고 장강이 홈그라운드인 수적들마저 표정이 환해졌다.
 10|
 11|물론 그중에서도 가장 기뻐하는 사람은 따로 있었다.
 12|
 13|“오오, 드디어…….”
 14|
 15|강제적인 재능기부로 호북성까지 오게 된 무송은 감격으로 몸을 부르르 떨었다.
 16|
 17|쾌조선 한 척이 침몰한 이후로 상심에 젖어 있던 그는 지금까지의 고생을 모두 잊은 듯 힘찬 목소리로 외쳤다.
 18|
 19|“닻을 내려라! 한시라도 빨리 이 지긋지긋한……!”
 20|
 21|만족스럽게 고개를 끄덕이고 있던 적천강이 무송을 바라보았다.
 22|
 23|“지긋지긋?”
 24|
 25|무심코 본심을 내뱉은 무송이 엄청난 속도로 고개를 저었다.
 26|
 27|“아, 아닙니다. 장강을 말한 겁니다.”
 28|
 29|“당연히 장강이지. 노부도 그런 뜻으로 한 말인데?”
 30|
 31|“…….”
 32|
 33|“설마, 우리를 두고 지긋지긋하다고 한 건가?”
 34|
 35|“그, 그럴 리가 있겠습니까.”
 36|
 37|상당히 그럴 리 있어 보이는데.
 38|
 39|적천강의 가늘어진 눈초리에 무송이 식은땀을 흘리는 동안 우두머리의 위기를 간파한 수적들은 잽싸게 움직였다.
 40|
 41|서서히 속도를 줄인 쾌조선들이 줄을 지어 정박하고 닻을 내리자, 항구 근처에 모여 있던 사람들 사이에서 작은 웅성거림이 일었다.
 42|
 43|“저 깃발은…….”
 44|
 45|“장강수로맹. 장강수로맹이다!”
 46|
 47|“밑에는 뭐라 적혀 있는 거야? 수룡채? 처음 들어보는데.”
 48|
 49|“사천에 본거지를 둔 수채일세. 해상왕의 둘째 제자인 선화아(船火兒) 무송이 맡은 수채가 바로 수룡채야.”
 50|
 51|“그렇게 말하니 들어본 것도 같군. 그런데 사천에 있어야 할 놈들이 왜 호북까지 온 거지?”
 52|
 53|“난들 어찌 알겠나. 빌어먹을 수적 놈들. 가뜩이나 요즘 들어 분위기가 흉흉한데…….”
 54|
 55|“쉿. 조용히 하게. 웬 젊은 놈이 이쪽을 보고 있어. 무림이랑 얽혀 봤자 좋을 게 없다고.”
 56|
 57|나와 시선이 마주친 상인 무리가 황급히 자리를 떴다.
 58|
 59|아니, 비단 그들뿐만이 아니었다. 얼굴이 새카맣게 탄 어부가 망을 챙겨 후다닥 물러나고, 잡은 물고기를 내다 팔던 장사치가 빛의 속도로 좌판을 접었다.
 60|
 61|저 멀리에서는 관복을 차려입은 벼슬아치는 관군들의 호위를 받으며 이쪽을 예의주시하고 있었다.
 62|
 63|그들의 눈빛에 서려 있는 것은 노골적인 경계심이었다.
 64|
 65|‘이거 어째…… 사천 쪽과는 분위기가 영 딴판인데?’
 66|
 67|장강수로맹이 제아무리 약탈을 근본으로 하는 수적 집단이라고 하지만 나름의 규칙과 체계가 잡혀 있다.
 68|
 69|건수가 있다 하면 달려들어서 닥치는 대로 죽이고 모조리 털어 가는 식이 아니라, 때로는 무근본 수적으로부터 선박을 보호하고 평소에는 일정량의 통행세만 받고 통과시킨다고 들었다.
 70|
 71|‘정마대전 당시에도 간을 좀 보긴 했지만 결국 정파 쪽에 붙었었고.’
 72|
 73|오는 것이 있으면 가는 것도 있는 법.
 74|
 75|장강수로맹은 천하 무림의 향방이 갈린 환란의 시기에 정파의 손을 들어 주었고, 관부에는 충분한 뇌물을 찔러 주었다.
 76|
 77|그렇다 보니 양쪽에서 묵인하고 넘어가는, 쉽게 말하자면 합법의 탈을 쓴 용역 깡패가 바로 장강수로맹이다.
 78|
 79|물론 그리 썩 좋은 놈들이라고는 할 수 없지만, 별의별 미친놈들이 날뛰는 무림 아닌가. 이 정도면 양반까진 아니더라도 그럭저럭 상놈 정도는 된다.
 80|
 81|‘그래서 사천에서는 양민들도 별다른 반응이 없었는데.’
 82|
 83|그냥 저 각설이 새끼들이 죽지도 않고 또 왔구나, 정도였지 지금처럼 대놓고 피하지는 않았다.
 84|
 85|나는 뿔뿔이 흩어지는 사람들을 보며 고개를 갸웃거렸다.
 86|
 87|‘지역마다 있는 분위기 차이. 뭐 그런 건가?’
 88|
 89|하지만 그런 것 치고는 슬쩍 바라본 무송의 표정이 심상치 않다.
 90|
 91|미간을 좁힌 채 순식간에 텅 빈 항구를 바라보던 그가 오른팔 격인 수하를 불렀다.
 92|
 93|“본 맹의 형제들에게서는 연락이 없느냐?”
 94|
 95|“예, 채주. 분명 우리가 오는 것을 알고 있었을 터인데, 어째서인지 아무 연통도 없습니다.”
 96|
 97|“당양채와 홍호채에서도?”
 98|
 99|“그렇습니다.”
100|
101|“다른 곳은 몰라도 동정채(東湖寨)는 황 숙부께서 계신 곳이다. 우리가 온 것을 그분이 모르셨을 리가 없는데…….”
102|
103|심각한 표정으로 중얼거린 무송이 수하를 향해 말을 이었다.
104|
105|“하선(下船) 후 날랜 놈들을 풀어 상황을 알아봐라. 인근의 형제들에게도 즉시 연락을 취하도록.”
106|
107|“존명.”
108|
109|무송의 손짓에 휘하 수적들이 일사불란하게 움직였다. 일찌감치 하선 준비를 끝마친 우리도 예외는 아니었다.
110|
111|드디어 장강을 벗어나게 된 적천강이 가장 빨리 앞장섰고, 그 뒤를 나와 진위경, 그리고 청풍과 혁무진, 궁기방이 차례대로 따랐다.
112|
113|있는 듯 없는 듯 조용히 사람들 사이에 녹아든 문경은 덤이다.
114|
115|드디어 상성 지역에서 벗어난 불 포켓몬, 적천강의 만면에 환한 웃음이 서렸다.
116|
117|“후우, 이제야 좀 살겠군. 이래서 사람은 땅을 밟고 살아야 한다니까.”
118|
119|하지만 적천강의 기쁨은 그리 오래가지 못했다.
120|
121|“거기 잠깐.”
122|
123|힘이 잔뜩 들어간 목소리. 어느새 다가온 벼슬아치가 우리를 바라보며 침을 꿀꺽 삼켰다.
124|
125|그리고 자신의 뒤에 서 있는 수백의 관군을 돌아보더니 가슴을 펴며 말을 이었다.
126|
127|“본관이 주위 말을 들어 보니 그대들이 사천에서 왔다던데. 맞나?”
128|
129|“그대들? 맞나?”
130|
131|눈을 껌뻑거린 적천강이 관리를 향해 되물었다.
132|
133|“혹시, 지금 그거 노부에게 한 말이냐?”
134|
135|“그렇다.”
136|
137|“그렇다?”
138|
139|관리의 눈빛이 불안하게 흔들렸다. 하지만 이내 마음을 다잡고 목소리를 키웠다.
140|
141|“어허, 본관이 묻는 말에만 대답하거라. 어디에서 왔는지, 또 무슨 목적으로 왔는지 낱낱이 고하지 못할까!”
142|
143|“어허? 하거라? 못할까?”
144|
145|“아, 아니 이 늙은이가…….”
146|
147|“늙은이?”
148|
149|안 돼. 하지 마. 제발 그만둬.
150|
151|훈남이 저렇게 되묻는 말투를 쓰면 여자들이 설렌다던데, 보는 사람 시선에서는 공포 영화가 따로 없다.
152|
153|나는 적천강이 저 권위적인 관리의 가슴에 화염 신장을 날리기 전에 잽싸게 끼어들었다.
154|
155|“저랑 이야기하시죠.”
156|
157|“대가리에 피도 마르지 않은 어린놈과 나눌 이야기는 없다!”
158|
159|“…….”
160|
161|호랑이 아가리에 들어갔던 거 꺼내 줬더니 말하는 꼬라지 보소.
162|
163|확 그냥 대가리를 날려 버리고 싶었지만, 꾹 참고 말을 이었다.
164|
165|“사천에서 온 거 맞고, 볼일이 있어서 왔습니다.”
166|
167|“하면, 그 볼일이라는 게 무엇이냐?”
168|
169|“그게…….”
170|
171|그 순간, 누군가가 잔뜩 신난 목소리로 외쳤다.
172|
173|“다진 고추를 듬뿍 얹은 생선찜이요!”
174|
175|“청풍, 이 개새끼야!”
176|
177|“왜요, 은인. 그거 진짜 맛있는데. 둘이 먹다 하나가 죽어도 모르는데…….”
178|
179|둘이 먹다 하나가 죽어도 모르는 맛인지는 몰라도, 관리의 눈에는 죽어야 할 놈들로 비친 것이 확실했다.
180|
181|얼굴이 시뻘게진 관리가 고래고래 외쳤다.
182|
183|“감히 본관을 능멸하다니!”
184|
185|“잠깐만, 아저씨. 그게 아니라…….”
186|
187|“장강수로맹의 깃발을 달고 사천에서 왔다는 것도 수상쩍기 짝이 없는데, 생선찜을 먹기 위해 와? 관을 봐야 눈물을 흘릴 놈들이로군. 여봐라, 당장 이 자들을 추포하라!”
188|
189|“명을 받드옵니다!”
190|
191|아니, 이 전개 뭔데.
192|
193|뭐라 할 새도 없이 벌어진 돌발 상황. 군기가 바짝 든 관군 수백 명이 창을 들고 우리를 에워싼 그때, 작게 혀를 찬 진위경이 앞으로 나섰다.
194|
195|“성질도 급하시구려.”
196|
197|진위경은 현대의 관점에서 봐도 장신이지만, 무림에서는 거인으로 통한다.
198|
199|우랄산맥 같은 어깨와 의복 위로 도드라진 근육을 바라본 관리가 마른침을 삼켰다.
200|
201|“그, 그대는 누군가?”
202|
203|“산서 태원진가의 진위경이라 하오. 긴말하지 않을 테니, 이쯤에서 수하들을 물리는 것이 어떻겠소?”
204|
205|관리가 뭐라 대답하기도 전에, 진위경의 묵직한 목소리가 이어졌다.
206|
207|“귀관이 아직 전달받지 못한 듯한데, 우리는 사천성주께 직접 통행을 허가받은 무림인들이오.”
208|
209|“……사천성주께서?”
210|
211|“미심쩍다면 확인해 봐도 좋소. 허나 그 전에 수하들을 물리는 것이 좋을 거요. 구태여 생목숨을 잃게 할 필요는 없을 테니.”
212|
213|관리는 물론이고 우리를 둘러싼 관군들의 창끝이 움찔 떨렸다.
214|
215|이들도 알고 있을 것이다. 자신들이 아무리 힘든 훈련을 거친 정예병이라고 해도 우리를 당해 낼 수 없다는 것을.
216|
217|하지만 원래 피는 아랫놈이 흘리고, 자존심은 윗놈이 강한 법이다. 관리의 눈에 바짝 힘이 들어가는 것이 보였다.
218|
219|“이자가 감히…… 본관이 누구인지 알고!”
220|
221|진위경은 표정 하나 변하지 않고 입을 열었다.
222|
223|“알고 있소. 호북성의 민정, 재정을 담당하는 승선포정사사에 적을 둔 건 당연할 테고. 관복을 보아하니 종육품 이문(理問)이시구려. 사법을 다루셔야 할 분께서 왜 여기까지 나와 애먼 사람을 붙잡고 있는지는 모르겠지만.”
224|
225|“……!”
226|
227|“아, 그건 그렇고 이 가에 홍천이라는 함자를 쓰시는 분을 알고 계시오?”
228|
229|관리의 입술 사이로 떨리는 목소리가 새어 나왔다.
230|
231|“그, 그분은 얼마 전에 새로 부임하신 포정사신데.”
232|
233|“그렇군. 얼핏 이야기를 들어 본 것도 같았지. 산서 육조참정에서 호북성 승선포정사라. 영전하신 셈이니 축하할 일이구려.”
234|
235|“호, 혹시 포정사님과 어떤 관계이신……?”
236|
237|진위경이 빙긋 웃었다. 어느새 그의 태도와 말투는 자연스럽게 관리를 내려다보고 있었다.
238|
239|“몇 번 만나 뵙고 술 한두 잔 했지. 필요할 때 도움도 드렸고.”
240|
241|“헉!”
242|
243|“왜. 더 듣고 싶은 말이 있나?”
244|
245|“아, 아닙니다!”
246|
247|빳빳하던 허리가 연체동물처럼 숙여졌다.
248|
249|진위경을 향해 잽싸게 폴더인사를 한 관리가 수하들을 향해 호통쳤다.
250|
251|“이놈들! 무엇 하느냐, 어서 그 흉한 날붙이를 치우지 않고!”
252|
253|“예, 옛!”
254|
255|“이런 경우도 모르는 놈들을 봤나! 부디 무례를 용서하십시오!”
256|
257|진위경이 자애롭게 관리의 어깨를 토닥여 주었다.
258|
259|“괜찮네. 살다 보면 오늘처럼 실수를 저지를 때도 있는 법이야.”
260|
261|“대해와도 같은 마음씨에 이 손 모, 감읍할 따름입니다!”
262|
263|“나 말고 이분들께 직접 사과드리게. 특히 자네가 처음 말을 걸었던 분은 무림의 존경받는 어른이시지.”
264|
265|“저, 저는 그런 줄도 모르고. 하오면 혹시 별호를 여쭤봐도…….”
266|
267|“화왕 적천강 대협이시네.”
268|

“It is suspicious enough that you came from Sichuan under the flag of the Yangtze River Channel League, and now you claim you came here to eat steamed fish? You’re the sort who won’t shed a tear until you see the coffin. Guards, arrest them at once!”

[P95]
“Yes, sir!”

[P96]
What the hell was this development?

[P97]
Before I could say another word, hundreds of well-drilled government troops raised their spears and surrounded us. Jin Wikyung clicked his tongue softly and stepped forward.

[P98]
“You’re rather quick-tempered.”

[P99]
Jin Wikyung was tall even by modern standards. In Murim, he was considered a giant.

[P100]
The official swallowed hard as he took in Jin Wikyung’s Ural Mountain shoulders and the muscles bulging beneath his clothes.

[P101]
“W-who are you?”

[P102]
“I am Jin Wikyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan in Shanxi. I won’t waste words, so why don’t you withdraw your men?”

[P103]
Before the official could answer, Jin Wikyung continued in his deep voice.

[P104]
“It seems you haven’t been informed yet, but we are martial artists who received direct permission to pass from the City Lord of Sichuan Province.”

[P105]
“The City Lord of Sichuan Province?”

[P106]
“If you doubt me, you may verify it. But before you do, I suggest you withdraw your men. There’s no need to throw away perfectly good lives.”

[P107]
The official flinched, and the spearpoints of the government troops surrounding us trembled.

[P108]
They knew it too. No matter how rigorous their training or how elite they were, they couldn’t defeat us.

[P109]
But that was how the world worked. The men at the bottom shed the blood, while the men at the top guarded their pride. I saw the official’s eyes harden.

[P110]
“How dare you… Do you even know who this official is?”

[P111]
Without the slightest change in expression, Jin Wikyung replied.

[P112]
“I do. Naturally, you belong to the Hubei Provincial Administration Commission, which oversees the province’s civil and financial affairs. Judging by your robes, you are a Judicial Inquirer of the secondary sixth rank. Though I don’t know why a man responsible for judicial affairs has come all the way out here to arrest innocent people.”

[P113]
“…!”

[P114]
“Oh, that reminds me. Do you know a man surnamed Yi, with the given name Hongcheon?”

[P115]
A trembling voice slipped between the official’s lips.

[P116]
“H-he is the Provincial Administration Commissioner who was newly appointed not long ago.”

[P117]
“I see. I thought I’d heard something about that. From Assistant Provincial Administrator in Shanxi to Provincial Administration Commissioner of Hubei. Quite the promotion. An occasion worth celebrating.”

[P118]
“M-might I ask what your relationship is with the Provincial Administration Commissioner?”

[P119]
Jin Wikyung smiled faintly. At some point, his posture and tone had naturally shifted into those of a man looking down at the official.

[P120]
“I’ve met him a few times and shared a drink or two with him. I also helped him when he needed it.”

[P121]
“Gasp!”

[P122]
“Why? Is there something else you’d like to hear?”

[P123]
“N-no, sir!”

[P124]
The official’s rigid back folded like a mollusk.

[P125]
After snapping into a deep bow toward Jin Wikyung, he spun around and roared at his subordinates.

[P126]
“You fools! What are you doing? Put away those vicious blades at once!”

[P127]
“Y-yes, sir!”

[P128]
“What sort of idiots can’t even read a situation like this? Please forgive our rudeness!”

[P129]
Jin Wikyung benevolently patted the official on the shoulder.

[P130]
“It’s all right. Everyone makes mistakes in life, like you did today.”

[P131]
“This man Son is deeply moved by your generosity, as vast as the sea!”

[P132]
“Don’t apologize to me. Apologize to these men directly. Especially the gentleman you addressed first. He is a highly respected elder of Murim.”

[P133]
“I-I had no idea. Then might I ask his sobriquet…?”

[P134]
“He is Great Hero Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King.”

[P135]
“…!”

[P136]
“We came straight to Hubei after the Sichuan Blood Tragedy, aboard a ship borrowed from the Yangtze River Channel League. Oh, and of course, we didn’t come solely to eat steamed fish.”

[P137]
*Stop it. You’re going to make him cry.*

[P138]
The official looked from one of us to another with an expression that said he wanted to die, performing the remarkable feat of bowing five times a second.

[P139]
Jin Wikyung nudged me lightly in the ribs.

[P140]
“What do you think, my youngest? Your big brother looked cool, didn’t he?”

[P141]
“You would’ve looked cool if you hadn’t said that.”

[P142]
“Once you establish connections with the government, they make many things more convenient. If you ever find yourself in trouble, try using my name.”

[P143]
If he could say that with such confidence, he must have planted quite a few seeds.

[P144]
According to Gung Gibang, the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s meteoric rise in such a short time was virtually unprecedented.

[P145]
If Jin Mukyung, who was undoubtedly continuing his grueling training at the Jin Family even now, was a martial arts genius, then Jin Wikyung was an all-rounder who possessed everything a Family Head needed.

[P146]
“My youngest, don’t you think I looked cool? Hm?”

[P147]
“…”

[P148]
Yes. Apart from things like this, he was the perfect Family Head.

[P149]
I was still trying to push away the increasingly clingy Jin Wikyung when it happened.

[P150]
“Everyone, stand aside.”

[P151]
At the deep voice infused with profound internal energy, the people murmuring some distance from the harbor parted to either side.

[P152]
At the same time, dozens of martial artists carrying considerable qi approached us with measured steps.

[P153]
*That’s…*

[P154]
I narrowed my eyes.

[P155]
Written in cloud-like calligraphy across their pure-white silk martial robes were the words:

[P156]
**Zhuge Clan.**

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). ## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

The swift ships gradually slowed, lined up along the pier, and dropped anchor. A murmur rose from the people gathered near the harbor.

[P21]
“That flag…”

[P22]
“The Yangtze River Channel League. It’s the Yangtze River Channel League!”

[P23]
“What does it say underneath? Water Dragon Stronghold? Never heard of it.”

[P24]
“It’s a river stronghold based in Sichuan. Water Dragon Stronghold is led by Ship-Fire Boy Mu Song, the Seafaring King’s second Disciple.”

[P25]
“Now that you mention it, I think I’ve heard of them. But why are those bastards in Hubei when they’re supposed to be in Sichuan?”

[P26]
“How should I know? Damn river bandits. Things have been tense enough lately as it is…”

[P27]
“Shh. Keep your voice down. Some young man is looking this way. Nothing good comes from getting tangled up with Murim.”

[P28]
The group of merchants who met my eyes hurried away.

[P29]
And they weren’t the only ones.

[P30]
A fisherman whose face had been blackened by the sun grabbed his net and scurried off, while a vendor selling his catch packed up his stall at the speed of light.

[P31]
In the distance, an official in formal robes watched us closely, surrounded by an escort of government troops.

[P32]
Their eyes held undisguised wariness.

[P33]
*What the hell? This atmosphere is completely different from Sichuan.*

[P34]
The Yangtze River Channel League might have been a band of river pirates founded on plunder, but it had rules and an established system of its own.

[P35]
I’d heard they didn’t simply pounce whenever they spotted an opportunity, kill everyone in sight, and strip the ship bare. Sometimes they even protected vessels from unaffiliated river bandits, and under normal circumstances, they only collected a set toll before letting ships pass.

[P36]
*They tested the waters during the Great Faction War, but in the end, they sided with the orthodox faction.*

[P37]
Give and take made the world go round.

[P38]
During the upheaval that decided the future of Murim, the Yangtze River Channel League had backed the orthodox faction and slipped the government enough bribes to keep it satisfied.

[P39]
In other words, they were hired thugs in a cloak of legality, tolerated by both sides and allowed to carry on.

[P40]
They couldn’t exactly be called good people, but this was Murim, where every kind of lunatic imaginable ran wild. They might not be gentlemen, but by Murim standards, they were at least run-of-the-mill scoundrels.

[P41]
*That’s why ordinary people in Sichuan barely reacted to them.*

[P42]
Their attitude had been more like, *Those beggar bastards are still alive and back again?* They certainly hadn’t openly avoided us like this.

[P43]
I tilted my head as I watched the people scatter in every direction.

[P44]
*Is it just a difference in atmosphere from one region to another?*

[P45]
But if that were all, Mu Song’s expression wouldn’t have looked so grim.

[P46]
He stared at the suddenly deserted harbor with a deep frown, then called over his right-hand man.

[P47]
“Have we received no word from our brothers in the League?”

[P48]
“No, Stronghold Lord. They must have known we were coming, but for some reason, there has been no contact.”

[P49]
“Not even from Dangyang Stronghold or Honghu Stronghold?”

[P50]
“That is correct.”

[P51]
“Even if the others didn’t know, Uncle Hwang is at Donghu Stronghold. There’s no way he failed to hear that we were coming…”

[P52]
Mu Song muttered with a grave expression, then continued.

[P53]
“Once we disembark, send out our fastest men to find out what’s happening. Contact our nearby brothers immediately as well.”

[P54]
“As you command.”

[P55]
At Mu Song’s gesture, the river bandits under his command moved as one. We were no exception, having finished our preparations to disembark long ago.

[P56]
Jeok Cheongang, finally leaving the Yangtze behind, led the way. I followed, then Jin Wikyung, Cheongpung, Hyuk Mujin, and Gung Gibang.

[P57]
Mungyeong came too, blending so quietly into the crowd that one could almost forget he was there.

[P58]
At last, Jeok Cheongang—the Fire Pokémon finally free of his type disadvantage—wore a radiant smile.

[P59]
“Whew. I can finally breathe again. This is why people are meant to live with their feet on solid ground.”

[P60]
But his happiness didn’t last long.

[P61]
“You there. Stop.”

[P62]
The voice strained with authority. An official who had approached us swallowed hard as he looked our group over.

[P63]
Then he glanced at the hundreds of government troops behind him, puffed out his chest, and continued.

[P64]
“I hear you came from Sichuan. Is that correct?”

[P65]
“‘You’? ‘Is that correct’?”

[P66]
Jeok Cheongang blinked and echoed the official’s words back at him.

[P67]
“Were you addressing this old man just now?”

[P68]
“That is correct.”

[P69]
“‘That is correct’?”

[P70]
The official’s eyes wavered uneasily. But he quickly steeled himself and raised his voice.

[P71]
“Ahem! Answer only what this official asks. State clearly where you came from and what purpose brings you here!”

[P72]
“‘Ahem’? ‘Answer me’? ‘State your purpose’?”

[P73]
“N-now listen here, old man…”

[P74]
“‘Old man’?”

[P75]
*Don’t. Don’t do it. Please, just stop.*

[P76]
They said women got butterflies when a handsome man repeated someone’s words like that, but from where I stood, this was a horror movie.

[P77]
I hurriedly stepped in before Jeok Cheongang could drive a Flame God Palm into the arrogant official’s chest.

[P78]
“Talk to me instead.”

[P79]
“I have nothing to discuss with some wet-behind-the-ears brat!”

[P80]
“…”

[P81]
I’d just pulled him out of a tiger’s jaws, and this was how he talked to me?

[P82]
I wanted to knock his head clean off, but I forced myself to hold back.

[P83]
“We did come from Sichuan, and we have business here.”

[P84]
“Then what business would that be?”

[P85]
“Well…”

[P86]
At that moment, someone shouted excitedly.

[P87]
“Steamed fish topped with lots of minced chili peppers!”

[P88]
“Cheongpung, you son of a bitch!”

[P89]
“Why, Benefactor? It really is delicious. It’s so good that if two people were eating it and one dropped dead, the other wouldn’t even notice…”

[P90]
I didn’t know if it was really delicious enough that one person could die without the other noticing, but from the official’s expression, it was clear that we looked like people who deserved to die.

[P91]
His face turned bright red as he bellowed.

[P92]
“How dare you mock this official!”

[P93]
“Wait, mister. That’s not what he meant…”

[P94]
“It is suspicious enough that you came from Sichuan under the flag of the Yangtze River Channel League, and now you claim you came here to eat steamed fish? You’re the sort who won’t shed a tear until you see the coffin. Guards, arrest them at once!”

[P95]
“Yes, sir!”

[P96]
What the hell was this development?

[P97]
Before I could say another word, hundreds of well-drilled government troops raised their spears and surrounded us. Jin Wikyung clicked his tongue softly and stepped forward.

[P98]
“You’re rather quick-tempered.”

[P99]
Jin Wikyung was tall even by modern standards. In Murim, he was considered a giant.

[P100]
The official swallowed hard as he took in Jin Wikyung’s Ural Mountain shoulders and the muscles bulging beneath his clothes.

[P101]
“W-who are you?”

[P102]
“I am Jin Wikyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan in Shanxi. I won’t waste words, so why don’t you withdraw your men?”

[P103]
Before the official could answer, Jin Wikyung continued in his deep voice.

[P104]
“It seems you haven’t been informed yet, but we are martial artists who received direct permission to pass from the City Lord of Sichuan Province.”

[P105]
“The City Lord of Sichuan Province?”

[P106]
“If you doubt me, you may verify it. But before you do, I suggest you withdraw your men. There’s no need to throw away perfectly good lives.”

[P107]
The official flinched, and the spearpoints of the government troops surrounding us trembled.

[P108]
They knew it too. No matter how rigorous their training or how elite they were, they couldn’t defeat us.

[P109]
But that was how the world worked. The men at the bottom shed the blood, while the men at the top guarded their pride. I saw the official’s eyes harden.

[P110]
“How dare you… Do you even know who this official is?”

[P111]
Without the slightest change in expression, Jin Wikyung replied.

[P112]
“I do. Naturally, you belong to the Hubei Provincial Administration Commission, which oversees the province’s civil and financial affairs. Judging by your robes, you are a Judicial Inquirer of the secondary sixth rank. Though I don’t know why a man responsible for judicial affairs has come all the way out here to arrest innocent people.”

[P113]
“…!”

[P114]
“Oh, that reminds me. Do you know a man surnamed Yi, with the given name Hongcheon?”

[P115]
A trembling voice slipped between the official’s lips.

[P116]
“H-he is the Provincial Administration Commissioner who was newly appointed not long ago.”

[P117]
“I see. I thought I’d heard something about that. From Assistant Provincial Administrator in Shanxi to Provincial Administration Commissioner of Hubei. Quite the promotion. An occasion worth celebrating.”

[P118]
“M-might I ask what your relationship is with the Provincial Administration Commissioner?”

[P119]
Jin Wikyung smiled faintly. At some point, his posture and tone had naturally shifted into those of a man looking down at the official.

[P120]
“I’ve met him a few times and shared a drink or two with him. I also helped him when he needed it.”

[P121]
“Gasp!”

[P122]
“Why? Is there something else you’d like to hear?”

[P123]
“N-no, sir!”

[P124]
The official’s rigid back folded like a mollusk.

[P125]
After snapping into a deep bow toward Jin Wikyung, he spun around and roared at his subordinates.

[P126]
“You fools! What are you doing? Put away those vicious blades at once!”

[P127]
“Y-yes, sir!”

[P128]
“What sort of idiots can’t even read a situation like this? Please forgive our rudeness!”

[P129]
Jin Wikyung benevolently patted the official on the shoulder.

[P130]
“It’s all right. Everyone makes mistakes in life, like you did today.”

[P131]
“This man Son is deeply moved by your generosity, as vast as the sea!”

[P132]
“Don’t apologize to me. Apologize to these men directly. Especially the gentleman you addressed first. He is a highly respected elder of Murim.”

[P133]
“I-I had no idea. Then might I ask his sobriquet…?”

[P134]
“He is Great Hero Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King.”

[P135]
“…!”

[P136]
“We came straight to Hubei after the Sichuan Blood Tragedy, aboard a ship borrowed from the Yangtze River Channel League. Oh, and of course, we didn’t come solely to eat steamed fish.”

[P137]
*Stop it. You’re going to make him cry.*

[P138]
The official looked from one of us to another with an expression that said he wanted to die, performing the remarkable feat of bowing five times a second.

[P139]
Jin Wikyung nudged me lightly in the ribs.

[P140]
“What do you think, my youngest? Your big brother looked cool, didn’t he?”

[P141]
“You would’ve looked cool if you hadn’t said that.”

[P142]
“Once you establish connections with the government, they make many things more convenient. If you ever find yourself in trouble, try using my name.”

[P143]
If he could say that with such confidence, he must have planted quite a few seeds.

[P144]
According to Gung Gibang, the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s meteoric rise in such a short time was virtually unprecedented.

[P145]
If Jin Mukyung, who was undoubtedly continuing his grueling training at the Jin Family even now, was a martial arts genius, then Jin Wikyung was an all-rounder who possessed everything a Family Head needed.

[P146]
“My youngest, don’t you think I looked cool? Hm?”

[P147]
“…”

[P148]
Yes. Apart from things like this, he was the perfect Family Head.

[P149]
I was still trying to push away the increasingly clingy Jin Wikyung when it happened.

[P150]
“Everyone, stand aside.”

[P151]
At the deep voice infused with profound internal energy, the people murmuring some distance from the harbor parted to either side.

[P152]
At the same time, dozens of martial artists carrying considerable qi approached us with measured steps.

[P153]
*That’s…*

[P154]
I narrowed my eyes.

[P155]
Written in cloud-like calligraphy across their pure-white silk martial robes were the words:

[P156]
**Zhuge Clan.**
